title: Monday, October 12: Osceola bridge closure, Oakdale street levy and bond cap, Helmo Station site, school results, county perimeter upgrade
summary:
Minnesota and Wisconsin Departments of Transportation, Hwy 243 Osceola Bridge. Late October 2026 through fall 2027. Detours via Hwy 8 or Hwy 36. Osceola Landing closed from Sept. 14 through late summer 2028. https://www.dot.state.mn.us/metro/projects/hwy243osceola/
Oakdale City Council, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 7 p.m., Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Avenue North. Street levy $975,871. Bond ceiling $18,600,000. Les Schwab Tire Center plat, parcel 1702921410011. https://www.oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10132026-920
Oakdale City Council workshop, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 5 p.m., Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Avenue North. Helmo Station site, about 8 acres. https://www.oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10132026-919
Stillwater Area Public Schools Board study session, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 5:30 p.m., Oak Park Learning Center, 6355 Osman Avenue North. Reading, math, and science results. https://meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Agenda/2592?meeting=769102
Washington County Board of Commissioners, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 9 a.m., Stillwater. Perimeter upgrade $1,083,920. County Road 50 and Highway 61 design $449,777.18. https://www.washingtoncountymn.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10132026-1951
script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, October 12. Here is the week's news.

The Hwy 243 Osceola Bridge over the St. Croix River is scheduled to close in late October 2026 through fall 2027.

Minnesota Department of Transportation is working with the Wisconsin Department of Transportation to replace the bridge, built in 1953, over the St. Croix National and Scenic Riverway. Detours run north on the Hwy 8 Taylors Falls River Crossing via Hwy 95, Hwy 8, Hwy 35 and Hwy 243, or south on the Hwy 36 Stillwater River Crossing using Hwy 95, Hwy 36, Hwy 64, Hwy 35, Hwy 64B, Hwy 35 and Hwy 243. The Osceola Landing north boat launch and parking lot is closed from 8 a.m. Monday, September 14 through late summer 2028. No dollar amount appears on the project page.

Oakdale's council meets Tuesday night on a nine hundred seventy-five thousand, eight hundred seventy-one dollar street levy that would leave the 2026 budget and come back in 2027.

That figure is debt-issuance levy money in the Streets Capital Improvement Fund for street projects R2026-01 and R2026-02. The amendment would cut it from 2026 revenue and put the same nine hundred seventy-five thousand, eight hundred seventy-one dollars into 2027, as reimbursement for those projects. A September 22 parameters vote allowed a bond sale of up to twenty million dollars. The restated sale drops the improvement bonds. The new ceiling is eighteen million, six hundred thousand dollars: eleven million, nine hundred thousand in sales-tax revenue bonds and six million, seven hundred thousand in capital-improvement bonds. The interest cap rises to six percent. Bids have to be for at least seventeen million, four hundred forty-nine thousand, two hundred seventy-five dollars plus accrued interest. The proposed sale date is October 22.

Les Schwab Tire Center wants a final plat on a vacant outlot north of Thirty-third Street North, parcel 1702921410011. The site is about seven point five acres. The buildable piece, about two point two acres, would hold an eight thousand, two hundred square foot building for tire sales and automotive service. The land is in the Oakdale Marketplace planned-unit district, guided mixed use. No variance and no city incentive are requested. The council approved the preliminary plat and site plan on August 25. Knights of Columbus Council number 4374 wants a bingo fundraiser on November 14 at Transfiguration Catholic Church, six thousand one hundred thirty-five Fifteenth Street North. Pavilion painting is listed at thirty-seven thousand, seven hundred five dollars. A public-safety traffic grant is listed at nineteen thousand, seven hundred fifty dollars. Claims on the agenda total two million, three hundred fifteen thousand, seven hundred ninety-five dollars and fifty-five cents. The meeting is at seven at the Discovery Center, forty-four forty-four Hadley Avenue North.

Oakdale's council workshop Tuesday is on an eight-acre Helmo Station site the Metropolitan Council owns beside the Gold Line station.

The land sits in the Helmo Station planned-unit district. The Metropolitan Council acquired it for the Gold Line. A warehouse that stood there has been demolished. About one acre on the south is a park-and-ride. About seven acres are left for redevelopment. The draft agreement is among the city, the city's Economic Development Authority, and the Metropolitan Council. It does not approve a developer, a financing package, or a property conveyance. Zoning and development approvals stay with the city. A later project would still need the usual council vote. Staff's timeline puts a council vote on the agreement at November 10. The workshop is at five at the Discovery Center, forty-four forty-four Hadley Avenue North.

Stillwater's school board meets Tuesday on this year's reading, math, and science results, and on a high school schedule the district already put in place.

The achievement report covers the district's goals under the state's Comprehensive Achievement and Civic Readiness law, and 2025-26 Minnesota Comprehensive Assessment results in reading, mathematics, and science. The agenda marks it information only. Stillwater Area High School started a redesigned schedule this school year to add courses and give students more flexibility. The presentation covers early results, who is in the new programming, and where the district sees room to improve. A course-proposal discussion is on the same list. A part-time teacher program resolution is on the agenda for review. Consent includes an Eagle Scout project to build wooden picnic benches for Stillwater Middle School, estimated at eight hundred dollars in materials. A closed session is listed to develop or consider an offer to buy or sell real property. The study session is at five-thirty at Oak Park Learning Center, sixty-three fifty-five Osman Avenue North.

Washington County commissioners meet Tuesday on a one million, eighty-three thousand, nine hundred twenty dollar contract for a combined perimeter upgrade at the Law Enforcement Center and a four hundred forty-nine thousand, seven hundred seventy-seven dollar and eighteen cent design for the County Road 50 and Highway 61 intersection.

Public Works asks the board to authorize a temporary four hundred fifty thousand dollar use of fund balance and to approve the Pember Companies contract for the perimeter project. A separate consent item asks for the HDR Engineering contract on the road design. Other consent items include a thirteen thousand, five hundred forty-eight dollar return of funds from Hennepin County, appointments to the Valley Branch Watershed District, a public hearing on the 2027 fee schedule, and resolutions on local road grants, snowmobile trails, and environmental charges. The agenda does not print the unpaid environmental-charge total, the three road-grant projects, the snowmobile grant amount, or the capital-plan figures. The board is scheduled for nine in the morning in Stillwater. Workshops follow on the 2027 legislative platform and the draft 2027-2031 capital plan.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
